newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FARM WORKERS CRITICISE S.AFRICAN EVICTIONS BILL.
newsitem.headline: FARM WORKERS CRITICISE S.AFRICAN EVICTIONS BILL.

text.p: Groups representing South African farm workers said on Tuesday a proposed law intended to protect them from eviction did not go far enough and they would put pressure on the ruling African National Congress to change it.

Members of the National Land Committee (NLC), an umbrella group of non-government organisations working with rural communities, told reporters the Extension of Security of Tenure Bill, introduced by Land Affairs Minister Derek Hanekom, made too many concessions to farm owners.
"We have serious reservations about the bill," NLC director Brendan Pearce said. "It is an evictions monitoring bill."

Hanekom has said the bill is intended among other things to protect farm workers, almost all of whom are black or Coloured (mixed race), from unjustified eviction by farm owners, who are almost exclusively white.
The anti-eviction clauses in the bill were modified following representations by the South African Agricultural Union (SAAU), which had described the clauses as a charter for squatters.
But NLC field worker Nicholas Matebese said rural communities in the Eastern Cape were unhappy with the legislation as it was now drafted.
"There seems to be a movement starting and we are going to fight this, we are going to ensure that farm workers get what they are entitled to," he said.
"We are going to ensure that the government responds appropriately... We are going to ensure that there is too much pressure (on the government)," Matebese said.
He added that rural communities might not vote for the ANC in the next election, due in 1999, if it failed to heed their complaints.
Pearce said the NLC had raised its concerns with Hanekom but had been told no substantial changes to the bill could be made.
